reviews.text: Boy or girl, man or woman, black or white, any audience member who has ever marveled at the Space Age of our national history will find much to love in Hidden Figures
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: This was a great historical film that shined a light on black excellency during one of the most important times in US history.
reviews.author: Justin Brown

reviews.text: Charming performances by an incredibly black cast make this sometimes redundant historical drama worth watching.
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: “Hidden Figures” is a polished Hollywood movie through and through, but the power and importance of its story along with the three central performances easily overshadow any hiccups.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: The right crowd-pleaser for the right time.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: This glossy historical celebration leans towards the sentimental, but is timely and important nonetheless.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Brilliant performances by Taraji P. Henson, Octavia Spencer, Janelle Monae and a first rate ensemble make this a not to be missed revelation and righting of American herstory...
reviews.author: Jennifer Merin

reviews.text: To me, the film speaks of simple respect, due to every person because he or she is human.
reviews.author: Hosea Rupprecht

reviews.text: It's a story of greatness demanding acknowledgement.
reviews.author: Ari

reviews.text: The film never relinquishes its tight focus on three remarkable individuals who repeatedly demonstrate that they, too, possess the right stuff.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Hidden Figures puts the familiar period-piece lens on an overlooked part of space history without glossing over the ugly bits while still feeling hopeful for what science and technology can achieve when the best and brightest can participate
reviews.author: Nathan Mattise

reviews.text: A feel good, crowd pleaser of a movie.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Any merely or largely "official" version of the political and historical issues bound up with these events, such as the filmmakers adopt, is fraught with contradictions.
reviews.author: Joanne Laurier

reviews.text: The movie features outstanding performances and pays tribute to three pioneering Black women who played a central role at NASA in the early 1960s during the "space race" between the United States and the Soviet Union.
reviews.author: Deesha Philyaw

reviews.text: Bring the whole family to see an uplifting film about three women whose contributions to NASA and space travel should not be ignored.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: It's a feel good, inspirational and entertaining film with winning performances across the board and an incredibly valuable history lesson.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: One of the main problems of the film is that it builds the drama in a very naive, very artificial, very intentional way. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: All the three leads were fantastic.
reviews.author: Avaryl Halley

reviews.text: Very nice and entertaining.
reviews.author: Andrew Galdi

reviews.text: A superb cast and a true-life story long overdue in the telling.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Hidden Figures presented three brilliant black women who just wanted to do their jobs.
reviews.author: Jenna Marotta

reviews.text: Hidden Figures is almost all preaching with very little movie to speak of, and what movie is there is so broad that much of the message falls flat.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: Do yourself a favor and see Hidden Figures. It's that good.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: Watching Taraji P. Henson, Octavia Spencer and Kansas City, Kansas homie Janelle Monáe bringing all to life is a "Hallelujah moment."
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: Hidden Figures will likely satisfy on the actress' strength, but Taraji -- and her audience -- deserve better than focus-grouped pablum.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: Overall, Hidden Figures is an inspiring, empowering feature with stellar performances and a strong social message at its core.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: It is the subtlety and universality of Hidden Figures which makes this a cinematic journey that stands apart from the pack; just like Katherine G. Johnson, Dorothy Vaughan and Mary Jackson.
reviews.author: Debbie Lynn Elias

reviews.text: It brings alive a time period in all its complexity.
reviews.author: Tish Wells

reviews.text: The three main actresses are fun, expressive, endearing and turn their characters' naive enthusiasm into a spontaneous emotional grip. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: Hidden Figures flows nicely and tells a heartwarming story about perseverance and triumph in the face of adversity.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: It has a reverence for its subjects that is so vital. Part of that is thanks to the incredible performances from the cast.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: Hidden Figures is more about race than the space race, both of which are conquered with grace and girl power.
reviews.author: Udita Jhunjhunwala

reviews.text: By and large, Hidden Figures keeps the focus on the bold, brave, brilliant heroines at its core, even going so far as to have a nuanced rebuke of typical modern naïve racism while Kristen Dunst washes pee off her hands.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: You'll find nothing stylistically groundbreaking here, but Melfi guides this feel-good drama with class and confidence.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: Hidden Figures tells the fascinating story of three women who have been overlooked by history with great performances and an easy going confidence that their material is worth it.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: I hope people see it and then go learn more.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: Hidden Figures' greatest asset is its marquee actresses, especially Henson and Spencer.
reviews.author: Phil Guie

reviews.text: Of all the movies I've seen in 2016, Hidden Figures, is one of the most rewatchable and it is one I am eager for friends and family to go and see.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: It's an important film to be sure, but also a well-written and well-acted piece that's as inspiring as it is entertaining. It made me laugh and cry, with an ending that made me want to get up and cheer.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: Go watch it not just for the story, but also the excellent performances by the cast.
reviews.author: S. Indra Sathiabalan

reviews.text: A tight script bounces along with warmth, nuance and a deep respect for the story it is telling, with three fantastic characters at the centre.
reviews.author: Joni Blyth

reviews.text: Director Theodore Melfi does a good job of letting the narrative do the heavy lifting; he's got a nicely retro eye, though one could argue the end result feels a touch sanitized.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: Hidden Figures is a brilliant film.
reviews.author: Amanda Greever

reviews.text: Uplifting and life-affirming.
reviews.author: Nathalia Aryani

reviews.text: Hidden Figures inspires hope; not only because the scenes that show the lone woman in heels standing amidst a sea of black ties, not just because the women running their chalks over blackboards to solve equation after equation...
reviews.author: Bedatri D. Choudhury

reviews.text: Hidden Figures presents a different angle to what it means to be Black in America and delivers it to a wide audience.
reviews.author: Li Lai

reviews.text: ...a celebration of women, of African-Americans, of marriage and family, of intellectual pursuit and practice, of patience in the face of opposition, of humble service and doing an exceptional job even when no one recognizes you or tweets about it.
reviews.author: Joel Mayward

reviews.text: The story itself needs no embellishment to be riveting and Theodore Melfi's direction is straightforward and unflashy, enlivened by a powerful soul original soundtrack by Pharrell Williams that captures the period feel.
reviews.author: Alexa Dalby

reviews.text: Here's a compliment you don't get to give often: This movie is really good, and it didn't even need to be!
reviews.author: Bob Chipman

reviews.text: It's a highly entertaining crowd-pleaser that brings these women to the forefront... These stories intersect in a seamless manner, with all three leads getting a chance to shine.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: It's a movie that reminds us that America is at its best when living up to the pluralistic standards that we as a nation all too often find elusive, but remains the benchmark by which we should strive.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: Hidden Figures tells a story of genuine heroes that has been shelved for far too long. It also serves as inspiration to a nation of little girls to never stop reaching for those stars.
reviews.author: Aaron Peterson

reviews.text: Hidden Figures shines a light on three real women who deserve great acknowledgement. The movie makes us want to learn more, which is a good thing, but it would be better if we felt better informed coming out of the theatre.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: [Janelle Monáe] is an irresistible, glittering diamond who effervesces even when she doesn't need to, and I sincerely hope her film offers double now that she's proven how insanely good she is as an actress.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: With strong performances from the three leads most notably Taraji P. Henson, "Hidden Figures" is entertaining enough to leave a nice smile on your face.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: A feel good movie about an important subject and a fascinating moment in our history.
reviews.author: Glynis Costin

reviews.text: It's a rousing, patriotic, feel-good picture, with terrific performances from Taraji P. Henson, Janelle Monaé, and Octavia Spencer.
reviews.author: Marcianne Miller

reviews.text: Through strong performances, sensitive direction and the strength of its source material, Hidden Figures transcends cliché to become a genuinely moving, inspirational tale of perseverance, strength and love.
reviews.author: Alexandra Heller-Nicholas

reviews.text: Director Theodore Melfi has harmoniously married the darkness of racism with feel-good values. Hidden Figures is suitable for all ages.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: While we know the outcome of the project, it is the journey these women travel that makes this such an engaging film.
reviews.author: Pamela Powell

reviews.text: "Hidden Figures" is compelling, full of heart, and engaging. It's a transforming story that balances humor with drama. A must-see film that allows important themes to play out and is both heartwarming and motivational.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: An inspirational and relevant crowd-pleaser that dutifully respects its characters and their various struggles.
reviews.author: Glenn Heath Jr.

reviews.text: ... a rousing, powerful film that praises and celebrates Black women in a way that's far too uncommon in today's society. Good. They deserve it.
reviews.author: Mikey Mason

reviews.text: The movie is beautiful to watch in part because of the tremendous work of cinematographer Mandy Walker, who captures a feeling of a time long gone. The music elevates the true story.
reviews.author: Lapacazo Magrira Sandoval

reviews.text: Hidden Figures is the perfect balm. It offers an optimistic view of how great this country can be when we unite behind a common cause. And it's a fun space adventure to boot.
reviews.author: Annalee Newitz

reviews.text: The best parts of the movie are, in fact, the three main characters. Taraji P Henson, Octavia Spencer, and Janelle Monae are each captivating by themselves. Combined, they're mesmerising. They interact naturally and they give the movie authenticity.
reviews.author: Damian Levy

reviews.text: ...proving that history and human society are more entertaining than the lives of lonely astronauts divorced from social context, who talk to themselves on another planet or float alone in space.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: ... a safe bet that offers something for everyone, in addition to being well accompanied by new songs by Pharrell. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Taraji P. Henson, Octavia Spencer and Janelle Monáe are what make this movie. They are the heart.
reviews.author: Andre Meadows

reviews.text: As the first major release of 2017, it's a little early to call Hidden Figures the feel-good movie of the year, but let's at least hope it sets the tone.
reviews.author: Megan Basham

reviews.text: A more optimistic than pessimistic message. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Here, we right an historical wrong, looking back at the important ... contributions that a group of three African-American women made to our nation's space program.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: So important, while also just really entertaining and really enjoyable...you can't help but feel for these women.
reviews.author: Steph Cozza

reviews.text: The ultimate value of Hidden Figures is couched in its ability to empower the viewer; it occasionally indulges in populist cinema's most frequent vice of uninhibited emotion but these moments, and our reactions, are always earned.
reviews.author: Lidiya Josifova

reviews.text: "Hidden Figures" provides a positive image of women as science researchers who were able to balance their personal and professional lives to achieve success.
reviews.author: Jana Monji

reviews.text: ... "Hidden Figures" acquires a potent presence, even if it would be stretching things to say it's a great movie. Still, historically, socially and culturally it may be remembered after the year's better films have faded into the recesses of memory.
reviews.author: Uri Klein

reviews.text: It's the quiet fierceness the actresses bring to these roles that make the work compelling.
reviews.author: Al Hoff

reviews.text: Even though Hidden Figures is overstuffed with plot points and has way too much going on to properly flesh out in its roughly 2-hour running time, the film deserves praise for putting some unknown heroes into the limelight
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Most of this country's history - like most Hollywood movies - has been written by white men. 'Hidden Figures' is a great reminder of the unsung African-American women who contributed to all our accomplishments.
reviews.author: Alexandra MacAaron

reviews.text: Hidden Figures tells the amazing true story of three women who were pioneers in the space program.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Happily, the government hires women for its space program. Otherwise, how would we get this remarkable film?
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: As far as the viewer goes, the story dates back to the 60s, but when you catch the tributes paid to the the real Johnson, Vaughan, and Jackson during the credit roll, you know that this story of triumph needed to be told, right here, right now.
reviews.author: Meena Iyer

reviews.text: Directed by Theodore Melfi, this fascinating, hugely watchable and eventually heart-warming story does occasionally lack subtlety but it's deservedly up for a Best Picture Oscar.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: The pragmatism that flows through Hidden Figures provides a beacon of hope in a modern era that feels marked by uncertainty and despair.
reviews.author: Soraya Nadia McDonald

reviews.text: ... strong performances by Henson, Spencer and Monae.
reviews.author: Joanne Soh

reviews.text: It strikes a careful balance in showing how things were, and what they could be.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: These are emotional and nuanced performances that powerfully deliver a reminder of just how ugly a world of prejudice is.
reviews.author: Keeva Stratton

reviews.text: Hidden Figures is a story of friendship and inspiration and a reminder to have faith in your abilities - and it's also two hours of guaranteed empowerment that will blast you straight towards your goals.
reviews.author: Rebecca Lewis

reviews.text: Watch this movie for the important story it tells - women standing up against racism and sexism in different and complex ways.
reviews.author: Shyama Krishna Kumar

reviews.text: Hidden Figures" is crowd-pleasing entertainment of vital history.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: The performances are warm and good-humored, without exception. It is absolutely an inspirational movie.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: Balancing each woman's story within the structure of the Space Race is deftly handled, as their workdays require them to give 110 percent and then go home and raise families.
reviews.author: Brooke Corso

reviews.text: Salutes the trailblazing achievements of three African-American women who worked behind the scenes at Nasa as 'human computers', doing the hard sums before electronic machines were up to the task.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: It's mostly fine but largely forgettable, with a script that suffers from flat characters and which treats its story less like the powerful drama it is and more like a straight line evenly peppered with plot points.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: Hidden Figures is smart, funny, beautifully acted and altogether entertaining. And essentially true. What else could you possibly want?
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: All things considered, "Hidden Figures" wraps some fairly radical themes -- three African-American women entrusted with important NASA jobs at a time (1961-1962) when Jim Crow was still the law of the land -- in a largely unradical package.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: ... terrific drama, eye-opening history, and a great lesson for Hollywood.
reviews.author: Sean Axmaker

reviews.text: There's nothing wrong with Hidden Figures, and uncomplicated movies like it. It's certainly doing good by shedding light on some figures who shouldn't remain hidden in history.
reviews.author: Rain Jokinen

reviews.text: This drama, which puts black women at its center, is so triumphant, highlighting both the brilliance and lives of three women whose stories have been neglected in history books, and at the same time it elevates the profile of three great actresses.
reviews.author: Candice Frederick

reviews.text: I liked Hidden Figures so much I went back to see it again. And I liked it just as much the second time.
reviews.author: Diane Pershing

reviews.text: It may be predictable but it's also one of the most uplifting and triumphant movies of the year.
reviews.author: John Hanlon

reviews.text: Taraji P. Henson, Octavia Spencer and Janelle Monáe are very, very hard to dislike.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: The film isn't always subtle, but a broad brush sometimes leaves behind a big, beautiful swath of color.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: A largely prosaically told reworking of the outsider-versus-the-system paradigm that gains piquancy from the story it has to tell and the vibrant personages at its centre.
reviews.author: Matt Wolf

reviews.text: Taraji P. Henson as Katherine Johnson grows more and more confident in each scene. Her gentle no-problem-sir demeanour melts away into pure passion.
reviews.author: Nathania Gilson

reviews.text: Hidden Figures is a rich and uplifting experience.
reviews.author: Paul Mount

reviews.text: It's a terrific story told with a lot of verve and charm.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: It's the sparkling individual components that comprise the ideal equation here, rather than any attempt to craft a new formula.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: A movie that is important, well-performed, and entertaining. It's a real crowd-pleaser, in other words.
reviews.author: Alex Doenau

reviews.text: Just like NASA is feeling its way around space, one rocket at a time, the women in Hidden Figures are launching minor revolutions on the ground, one mathematical formula at a time.
reviews.author: Nandini Ramnath

reviews.text: Hidden Figures is engaging, entertaining and enlightening -- but by playing fast and loose with historical fact, it risks blunting some of the story's eye-opening emotional force.
reviews.author: Rob Garratt

reviews.text: In the two years since Margot Lee Shetterly's non-fiction book was optioned, the film's reflection on privilege feels even more relevant.
reviews.author: Roe McDermott

reviews.text: "Hidden Figures" is a rousing story of unsung heroism adapted with the mass appeal of a colouring book.
reviews.author: Blake Howard

reviews.text: Very uplifting.
reviews.author: Aine O'Connor

reviews.text: The title is an amazing pun, based on black women working at NASA -- and the calculations they made to help the space race.
reviews.author: Camilla Long

reviews.text: Well, I know which film I'll be rooting for come Oscar night.
reviews.author: Henry Fitzherbert

reviews.text: This splashy, feelgood period piece is every bit as enjoyable as a best picture Oscar-nominated blockbuster could hope to be.
reviews.author: Simran Hans

reviews.text: Almost every one of the fudges makes the film more entertaining and less truthful.
reviews.author: Paul Byrnes

reviews.text: Despite the stellar cast, though, the film is weighted down by an overload of subplots.
reviews.author: Rashid Irani

reviews.text: Hugely engaging, as well as important and inspiring.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: No people have ever deserved their own movie more than they do. And what a lovely movie this is.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: As [Melfi] proved in his previous film, St Vincent, he's good with actors and is a competent storyteller, but he can't resist underlining things that are already obvious.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: A heart-warming film and not one to be missed if you have lately been running low on inspiration in life. Let the stories of three geniuses tell you how a woman, despite several hurdles, can still cross the finish line.
reviews.author: Soumya Srivastava

reviews.text: Directed with Oscar-baiting flourish by Theodore Melfi, Hidden Figures works well as a well-meaning, corrective history lesson designed to honour the talented women who worked away in historical silence while castigating the system that oppressed them.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Even if some details have been massaged to fit the template of a Hollywood crowd-pleaser, the main thrust of the story is true and all the more remarkable for that.
reviews.author: Stella Papamichael

reviews.text: Yes, the story may have been panel-beaten into a gleaming, Oscar-friendly shape. That Hidden Figures is still so entertaining and moving is due in large part to a hugely likeable central trio of performances.
reviews.author: Ed Potton

reviews.text: This is an immensely likeable film and one that draws overdue attention to a story that has been neglected for far too long.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: Melfi's option for a brazenly feelgood formula could have easily undermined quite what a brutally obstructive status quo these women were facing up to but - thanks to trio of terrific performances - this is never an issue.
reviews.author: Tim Evans

reviews.text: Hidden Figures is light on its feet, warm-hearted and determined to entertain as well as educate.
reviews.author: Allan Hunter

reviews.text: Hidden Figures completes its mission by landing a deeply touching and buoyant story that shoots for the stars.
reviews.author: Laura Delaney

reviews.text: Hidden Figures is not a good movie. Sorry, but it's not.
reviews.author: David Jenkins

reviews.text: It's touching, sobering, sometimes funny, this lesson in racial history ...
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: This is heartfelt and inspiring stuff.
reviews.author: John Bleasdale

reviews.text: Hidden Figures isn't pushing the cinematic boat out in any new directions, but it steers its prescribed course nimbly and nicely.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: A remarkable biopic that demonstrates how holding back the tide of equality is detrimental to us all.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: You'd need to have a cold stone heart - or, I suppose, prejudicially racialist views - to dislike Hidden Figures ... A wonderful, rather incredible story, full of triumphant moments and performed by a perfect cast.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: Hidden Figures chronicles the trials and tribulations of these trailblazing women at an extraordinary time in human history.
reviews.author: Vicky Roach

reviews.text: Melfi's cast are so cool, and this truly is a story that should be told, particularly while race and gender are still such burning issues.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: Race and gender politics enter as small, personal insults -- a segregated coffee pot, a condescending smirk, a closed meeting-room door -- but every setback is tied up neatly with a victory.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: The performances here are wonderful and it is undoubtedly a "feel good" film with its warmth, vitality and empowering energy.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: A terrific film in the style of Hollywood 'applause' films, where the heroes or heroines are portrayed as not only morally superior but endlessly likeable
reviews.author: Andrew L. Urban

reviews.text: It's a great, uplifting story filled with 'firsts' at a time in the 60s when segregation was rife, women's roles were compromised and the NASA space program was keenly competing against the Russians ... Three delightful performances bring the women to life
reviews.author: Louise Keller

reviews.text: An old-fashioned story about discrimination and overcoming; inspiring, hopeful and impeccably acted. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Essentially Parabolas & Prejudice, it isn't the most nuanced piece of work out this month. But nuance be damned - an uplifting plea for equality, this is a story calibrated for maximum effect.
reviews.author: Nick De Semlyen

reviews.text: The pacey script is as slickly engineered as a Mercury rocket to include girl-power fun, romance and against-the-clock launchpad crises.
reviews.author: Kate Stables

reviews.text: While anger-inducing, Melfi ensures this film just about remains uplifting and inspiring, without compromising on the severity of the themes being explored.
reviews.author: Stefan Pape

reviews.text: Hidden Figures isn't nearly as revolutionary or convention-busting as its subjects, but it illuminates an important story, and is given flight by three charismatic performers.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: It's helpful that the acting trio sell the somewhat saccharine story well.
reviews.author: Amy West

reviews.text: A simple and extremely enjoyable film, one that brings smiles and keeps them for the rest of the day. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fausto Ponce

reviews.text: The sheer energy of the cast of Hidden Figures and the pure curiosity provoked by its subject are simply too warm and inviting to resist.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: A classic biopic with great one liners, endearing characters and a great cast. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro Alemán

reviews.text: The actual story of a group of African-American employees working for NASA in the late 1950s in the segregationist state of Virginia deserved a better movie. In any case, much more complex. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ernesto Diezmartinez

reviews.text: A film that fulfills its goal is to entertain with a real story of overcoming and prodigy of those who really inspire and invite you to know the real story once the credits begin to rise. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emmanuel Báez

reviews.text: An elegantly elaborate film with a script that marks the perfect balance between serious historical drama and entertainment. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Fernando Galván

reviews.text: A completely motivational story, which we might well consider anti-Trump, because it's a group of African-American women helping to fulfill a country's mission to reach the stars. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mario P. Székely

reviews.text: A biopic that is characterized by being entertaining, full of nuances that highlight familiar situations and it doesn't decay at any time creating boredom, nor in wants to victimize its protagonists. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Israel Acosta Aroche

reviews.text: A conventional and optimistic story that has the merit of showing the contribution of the three women to North America. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: Too bad that the film doesn't have more rage, reaction and resistance. A real pity. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Hidden Figures is not a particularly sharp or revealing film about race relations in the United States. However, the current conjuncture of that country allows these "talents" to take effect, but not transcendence. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge (JJ) Negrete

reviews.text: An irresistible and entertaining film that is effective in its objectives. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: Including some fine acting, the film is easy to appreciate and digest, without ever becoming preachy. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: A film with a powerful cast, remarkable emotional strength, closeness freshness and breathtaking vitality. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Javier Porta Fouz

reviews.text: A film that works because of the chemistry of its cast, the successful formula of feel-good movies and those inspiring stories that leaves you in a good mood. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Lucero Solórzano

reviews.text: A sort of familiar biopic, something according to the predictable and already marked milestones that frame its footage, and conducive to combine the effect of entertainment with instruction. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ignacio Navarro

reviews.text: By skillfully avoiding polemical statements and scenes of high drama, ... the film sends a powerful message about the evils of racism.
reviews.author: Richard James Havis

reviews.text: Looking for an entertaining film starring women of colour dominating an intellectual field? Then skip this review and watch Hidden Figures right bloody now.
reviews.author: Liam Maguren

reviews.text: A conventional but very curious and amusing biopic with an interesting story and the added attraction of revealing little-known events and characters from American history. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pilar Ayuso

reviews.text: A film that reveals the stories of its protagonists in three well compartmentalized plots and as calculated towards its objective as the trajectory of a space flight. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jordi Costa

reviews.text: In spite of its calculated excess of superficiality, it's an interesting, entertaining and very well interpreted film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Luchini

reviews.text: The story is a good one, and the movie never feels too heavy or preachy.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: It's not intended to be the definitive film about what it addresses, but it's a fairly close approach and anyone can enjoy it. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: The true story of three patient and patriotic African-American women who make an invaluable contribution to the success of the early space program.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: Hidden Figures doesn't try to push many artistic boundaries, but it tells its story so well that it doesn't really have to.
reviews.author: Lenika Cruz

reviews.text: We might already know the end of the film, which tends to feel a bit formulaic at times, but it still sucks us in. It's a feel-good story that's every bit worth rooting for.
reviews.author: Michelle Jaworski

reviews.text: With some audacity and ingenuity, "Hidden Figures" might have been something extraordinary. Instead, it's merely about something extraordinary.
reviews.author: J. Olson

reviews.text: If the currently released "Jackie" has an edge in glossy production design, the heart and soul of this film makes it stand a full head taller.
reviews.author: Ron Wilkinson

reviews.text: It's the kind of movie where you compliment the performances and then trail off because there's nothing much left to say that won't make you sound like a jerk.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: Uplifting, if not a little heavy handed, "Hidden Figures" is based on the true story of three very remarkable women and all three stars make the wise choice of not being stereotypical in their performances
reviews.author: Michael A. Smith

reviews.text: It [Hidden Figures] makes our eyes wander and our ears perk, always on the look out for those who may next pioneer us into greater, undiscovered territories.
reviews.author: Allyson Johnson

reviews.text: With any luck, Hidden Figures will bring viewers to the nonfiction account by Margot Lee Shetterly on which it's based -- and serve as an inspiration for STEM-minded kids who rarely see parallels to themselves on film.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: Three heroic African-American women carry this true NASA story to the heights of crowd-pleasing. The recent death of living legend/astronaut John Glenn adds even more heft to a movie that should serve as an inspiration to anyone who perseveres.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: its story of triumph over adversity is not so much a historical lesson as it is a call to ensure that we stop making the same old mistakes
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: A historical and pastel color drama that focuses in social awareness and sentimentality. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel de Partearroyo

reviews.text: Hidden Figures isn't a ground-, ceiling-, door-, or wall-breaking movie, but it entertains through its cast's charm.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: This is a movie that should be seen featuring a story that needed to be told.
reviews.author: Kristian Harloff

reviews.text: It's an uplifting cinematic experience that virtually anyone can enjoy, all while learning a story that deserved to be told.
reviews.author: Mark Ellis

reviews.text: Hidden Figures is a great time at the theater.
reviews.author: Andy Crump

reviews.text: ... inspirational but predictable celebration of sacrifice, can-do spirit of three exploited NASA workers ... feels pat, too self-aware ... may be overdoing things to redress past sins.
reviews.author: Glenn Lovell

reviews.text: The film's light, breezy entertainment value hides a deeper poignance, making it a nice complement to the heavier films that take the opposite approach.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: Hidden Figures deserves consideration as another great black hope of putting that #OscarsSoWhite problem to rest. More importantly, it's a lesson that African-American culture offers more inspiring stories than Hollywood has chosen to tell.
reviews.author: Steve Persall

reviews.text: It's as uplifting as watching a rocket take off.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: Three strong, brilliant black women doing it for themselves by forcing a racist, sexist government agency to swallow a little Jim Crow in order to take America to the stars and back.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: Three women of color transcended the boundaries of their time. They rose above a segregated, sexist society to show that intellect is color blind and gender neutral. Hidden Figures is a long overdue story.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: A lovely movie, buoyed by understated performances.
reviews.author: Rich Heldenfels

reviews.text: Smart and sweet, the movie doesn't so much press viewers to examine their own potential prejudices as it assumes the persuasive power of its own vision.
reviews.author: Cynthia Fuchs

reviews.text: It's pretty much perfect, and I cannot wait for general audiences to get the opportunity to head to the theatre and learn that blissful truth for themselves.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Taraji P. Henson, Octavia Spencer and Janelle Monáe bring every ounce of their considerable charm to a script filled with humor and heart.
reviews.author: Samantha Miller

reviews.text: Yes, the movie is idealized in its portrait of women who have undoubtedly been denied very ordinary human flaws and failings. But then, so what? They're heroes, every one of them.
reviews.author: Jeff Simon

reviews.text: If Quentin Tarantino really only has two movies left, I pray that at least one of them stars Janelle Monáe.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: The film is dominated by the energetic and often moving performances of its three leads, and bolstered by the quieter but still excellent work of the supporting players.
reviews.author: Allison Shoemaker

reviews.text: Of the formidable threesome, it's Monae who most stands out.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: Hidden Figures may be the most entertaining civil rights movie I've ever seen.
reviews.author: Christopher Lawrence

reviews.text: Despite admirable efforts from its high-powered cast, Hidden Figures takes a remarkable story and makes it feel the same as so many other movies.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: We learn about a largely unknown venue of the civil rights movement, but we also gain a general appreciation for the Herculean task of getting the Mercury astronauts into space at all.
reviews.author: Josh Terry

reviews.text: Hidden Figures is the rare true story-based historical drama that succeeds at being as inspirational and feel-good as it aspires to be.
reviews.author: Sandy Schaefer

reviews.text: An assertion of humanity and civil rights that is pure cinematic nourishment for soul.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: A by-turns infuriating and rousing feel-good drama.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: Brings to light a little-known facet of the American space program that simultaneously represents the best and the worst of what America had to offer at the time.
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: ... in light of national pride and recent politics, it's refreshing to see a film that shows individuals not only can work together but often enough had damn well better.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: Not enough can be said about the effort Henson, Monáe or Spencer put in. The three have impeccable chemistry and build their characters from the ground up, indelibly.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Imagine The Help meets The Right Stuff and you get a very good sense of which buttons and emotional thrusters director Melfi is using to guide his plastic model of a moon rocket.
reviews.author: Katherine Monk

reviews.text: With its by-the-numbers storytelling, 'Hidden Figures' has all the right stuff to enlighten the audience.
reviews.author: Roger Tennis

reviews.text: Hidden Figures succeeds where other movies have failed in making mathematical equations interesting.
reviews.author: Mal Vincent

reviews.text: It's a good family film in the sense that it probably won't upset anyone, but it's hard to escape the suspicion the real people on whose stories it is based deserve a more nuanced treatment.
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: The story that Hidden Figures tells is so irresistible that you can almost forgive the fact that the movie itself is resistibly unoriginal.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: Considering it could be an inspirational calling card for girls and kids of all colors to brandish their smarts in the world of science and math, that only makes it all the better. (Full Content Review for Parents - Profanity, etc. - also Available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Square but rousing portrait of real-life figures who helped U.S. win Space Race. Great cast.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Underneath convention is an inspection of tremendous intelligence finding its place in the world, with the production valuing education and problem solving, which doesn't come across the screen nearly enough.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: In 2017, when the country feels as angry and divided as ever, "Hidden Figures" becomes more than just a well-made, inspiring and rousing piece of entertainment. It becomes vital.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: ...an unabashedly feel-good movie, setting obstacles before its heroines and then showing their triumphs, while also offering the delights of a well-done period film.
reviews.author: Sarah Boslaugh

reviews.text: Johnson, Vaughan and Jackson were trailblazers whose fight deserves to be heard, and "Hidden Figures" honors them by turning their story into an audience-pleaser.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: A movie about great people is not the same thing as a great movie.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: Hidden Figures soars in bringing their stories to light and it's long past due.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: Hidden Figures is triumphant in a way that can restore your faith in the dreams we can achieve in this nation if we all are willing to work together as one.
reviews.author: Michael Smith

reviews.text: It's clear that Hidden Figures is a story that demands to be told, and it's a pity it wasn't told better.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: Hidden Figures celebrates the achievements of these accomplished women, not only as pioneers in the space race but also as heroes battling obstacles big and small.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Hidden Figures is exactly the type of movie that you think that it is. Only, it's better at being that type of movie than you probably expected.
reviews.author: Sean O'Connell

reviews.text: The film hews closely to the facts in important respects, and evokes the outrages of the Jim Crow era, as well as the feverish competition of the space race, through the fascinating work of its extraordinary heroines.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: Hidden Figures is a mash-up of the space race and civil rights that serves both well.
reviews.author: Jim Slotek

reviews.text: "Hidden Figures" is more than just an inspirational history lesson. It does the vital service of bringing long-ignored figures out of hiding and making their case to the world.
reviews.author: Loey Lockerby

reviews.text: This overeager, if oddly satisfying film details what it took for the U.S. to put a man in space at the height of the Cold War with Russia
reviews.author: Ken Eisner

reviews.text: It's consistently good, very well acted, and it introduces us to a group of patriots previously overlooked.
reviews.author: Edward Johnson-Ott

reviews.text: Both a dazzling piece of entertainment and a window into history ...
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: This affecting story of reclaimed history is something to enjoy and celebrate with family members of all generations.
reviews.author: Marjorie Baumgarten

reviews.text: Solving institutional discrimination has proven to be harder than getting John Glenn to circle the globe. But Hidden Figures focuses on people, not numbers or policies or platitudes.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: The story is compelling and the acting is very good in this historical drama about three women who succeeded in grand style against very long odds.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Hidden Figures is a crowd-pleaser in the purest sense - it's a charming, heartwarming and inspirational tale that skillfully combines light-hearted comedy with racially-charged drama.
reviews.author: Jason Zingale

reviews.text: Director Theodore Melfi ... creates an atmosphere in which Johnson, Vaughan and Jackson must be twice as good as those around them simply to succeed.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Melfi tends to paint too much in the broad, amiable strokes of a triumph-of-the-week TV movie. But even his earthbound execution can't dim the sheer magnetic pull of an extraordinary story.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: "Hidden Figures" is a feel-good film of incalculable charm.
reviews.author: Calvin Wilson

reviews.text: Goes beyond calling out prejudice because "it's wrong" and into its willfully ignorant blindness to bigger pictures of potential or accomplishment. It sees how cultural perseverance factors into much larger equations & earns inspirational bona fides.
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

reviews.text: Henson, Spencer and Monáe all bring spunk, sass and heart to a story that oozes inspiration and rings with righteous pride.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: Executed with love and peopled with actors who breathe life into their characters ... "Hidden Figures" is precisely the delight it aims to be.
reviews.author: Barbara VanDenburgh

reviews.text: The film's made with more heart than art and more skill than subtlety, and it works primarily because of the women that it portrays and the actresses who portray them.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Spencer gets most of the laughs, and Monáe has the showiest speeches, so they've been nominated for most of the awards. But Henson has the hardest role: a prodigy ill-used by a society that barely knows she's alive.
reviews.author: Lawrence Toppman

reviews.text: It's both a vital and important piece of our history and a strikingly slapdash movie, clumsily executed and filled with scenes that are barely half-written, if that. These two facts can co-exist. One may matter more to you than the other.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: A rousing, uplifting tribute to three unsung American heroes. Splendid performances give the film full power.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: It might not leave an award-season mark, but its blend of heart, humor and history should score where it counts the most: at the box office, and in the minds of young viewers.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: A triumph, that never feels like homework or a history lesson (Splice Today)
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: ...a beautifully crafted film...
reviews.author: Sophia Watson

reviews.text: Could hardly be more historically important, culturally significant, or inspirational, and as a PG-rated film, it's especially valuable as a STEM education boost for young girls.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: Melfi never loses sight of his heroines' dual struggle, as women and as black people. He encourages his actors to play on that duality with wisdom, anger, and a nuanced sort of farce.
reviews.author: Michael Sragow

reviews.text: ...a rare glimpse of the black experience as it pertains to wider American history.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: A potent film with strong performances that will bolster your belief that change can still be made with the right level of conviction.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: Paint-by-numbers biopic about people who were almost beyond a shadow of a doubt more interesting than the film ever suggests.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Surprising and Uplifting
reviews.author: Diana Saenger

reviews.text: ... a valuable history lesson with plenty of built-in drama that eventually takes off.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: This untold story of African-American females who helped NASA conquer the cosmos features three incredible performances. Corny at times, sure, but you'll still want to stand up and cheer.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: This gloriously entertaining slice of American history will make you want to stand up and cheer. In many ways, it is just the movie we need right now.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: Despite at least one counterfactual scene and a runtime far too long, it's an interesting and intriguing tale and writer Margo Lee Slatterly, along with director Theodore Melfi, deserve a lot of plaudits for bringing the story to light.
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: Tells a genuinely compelling story, but does so in a fashion that too often feels artificial, even borderline sitcomish [though] it's hard to resist the charm of the three lead actresses.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: A worthwhile, teachable moment about the indignities suffered by three heroic NASA mathematicians simply because they had the misfortune to be black during the South's shameful days of Jim Crow segregation.
reviews.author: Kam Williams

reviews.text: This film is designed to rouse an audience, and I can't see how it can fail to do so. The heroines of this tale are both admirable and likable, what the movie may lack in nuance it makes up for in good will
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: This movie is as much about science-faction, as it is a tense racial drama and a light-hearted comedy. It's an education film that should be mandatory viewing for the whole family.
reviews.author: Valerie Complex

reviews.text: Hidden Figures has a lot of fine lines to walk, and it does so with grace and grit equal to the trio of stellar performances from Henson, Spencer, and Monáe.
reviews.author: Roxana Hadadi

reviews.text: ...it's ultimately difficult to recall a more promising endeavor that so thoroughly squandered its various positive attributes.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Junior high and high school classes across the country should take field trips to see this movie.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Hidden Figures provides an example of determination and talent triumphing over an unfair and repressive system - something that ... has relevance beyond the decade or the century in which it transpires.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: The film's immensely agreeable real-life story has so much joy and energy, we're willing to go the predictable distance.
reviews.author: Anita Katz

reviews.text: Hidden Figures is charming, smart, capable, and uncompromising -- just like its subjects.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: Ultimately, it is a very satisfying movie, with historical significance, and it is great to see these women finally get their due.
reviews.author: Neil Rosen

reviews.text: Heartwarming, inspiring.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: Thoroughly entertaining with terrific performances all around.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: Strong female characters spitting in Jim Crow's eye. Hearkens back to the feel-good, morally-upright films of an earlier day.
reviews.author: Kimberly Gadette

reviews.text: [A] significant story, told well and with feeling.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: For all that it tells a highly unusual story, Hidden Figures is a classic Hollywood feel-good movie.
reviews.author: Kate Taylor

reviews.text: Taraji P. Henson, Octavia Spencer and Janelle Monáe serve both history and the demands of popular entertainment with serious performances that also have a good sense of humour.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: A distaff counterpart to The Right Stuff, this exuberant, inspiring drama tells the fact-based story of three black women who strove for upward mobility -- both professional and atmospheric.
reviews.author: J. R. Jones

reviews.text: I kept wishing director Theodore Melfi had approached his trio's story with the respect it deserves. Instead, he keeps trying to make their struggle "fun," chasing easy laughs and easy inspiration.
reviews.author: John Powers

reviews.text: In broad but mostly satisfying terms, Hidden Figures celebrates the few African-American women who broke out of the West Area Computers building because their talent was no longer worth suppressing.
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: The it's-about-damn-time true story that puts paid to the notion that only white men had the Right Stuff. Often funny, ultimately feel-good, hugely exhilarating.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: Adding social issues to its many inspirational themes, Hidden Figures equals one satisfying slice of history that'll entertain adults as well as kids looking to the stars.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: Like the calculating women whose lives it celebrates, "Hidden Figures" knows what it's doing.
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: There is something to be said for a well-told tale with a clear moral and a satisfying emotional payoff.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: ...pays worthy tribute to their brilliance and determination in the face of overwhelming social odds, and does so in a way that engages emotionally.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: This is old-fashioned storytelling at its best: a tear-jerker and a feel-good movie all in one.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Edalatpour

reviews.text: As a reminder of what can happen when Americans pull together behind a collective and ambitious cause, it's welcome, a rejoinder to the great strife and division that permeates the national mood today.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: This movie adroitly portrays the sheer waste and inefficiency of racism and misogyny. Just think how much has been lost, the movie suggests, over centuries of depriving ourselves of the brains, talents and leadership of more than half our population?
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: "Hidden Figures" is a fairly entertaining gloss of a docudrama elevated by its cast.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: "Hidden Figures" may be a thoroughly upbeat, entertaining movie, but it's too smart to sugarcoat the truth about race relations in America - past or present.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: The miracle lies in how the film gently touches on some of the most intractable social problems addressed by the civil rights movement, while maintaining an infectiously buoyant vibe - not to mention a bouncy soundtrack.
reviews.author: Tirdad Derakhshani

reviews.text: Inspiring true story of African-American women at NASA.
reviews.author: Sandie Angulo Chen

reviews.text: Timeliness shouldn't ever be a mark for excellence. But the barndoor broad "Hidden Figures" would likely be entertaining at any time.
reviews.author: Matt Prigge

reviews.text: I expect that anyone can find inspiration in the script's attention to the small, concrete steps real people make to create change.
reviews.author: Alan Scherstuhl

reviews.text: The film aims for the stars but might have gone stratospheric if it cooled its jets ever so slightly.
reviews.author: Joshua Rothkopf

reviews.text: Hidden Figures does a remarkable job demonstrating that women may all want different things but all desire opportunity.
reviews.author: Lauren Chval

reviews.text: It is in essence a feature-length version of an inspiring social media image macro, or perhaps a Google Doodle.
reviews.author: Dan Schindel

reviews.text: Taraji P. Henson, Octavia Spencer and Janelle Monáe are irresistible (and unstoppable) in this engaging story of pioneering black female mathematicians at NASA.
reviews.author: Kevin Lally

reviews.text: "Hidden Figures" provides a fresh angle on how demeaning, demoralizing and crazy it was to live in an era of officially sanctioned white supremacy, one that people had grown used to pretending was perfectly normal.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Theodore Melfi has a light touch not often found in dramas like this, which makes the material all the more effective.
reviews.author: Odie Henderson

reviews.text: Henson, Spencer and Monae all excel, conveying the intensity and worthiness of these women's ambitions, even as they deal, almost in a matter of fact way, with obstacles that are maddening.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: For all of its current touchstones, Hidden Figures feels far too late, both in the recognition these women deserve and the filmmakers' goodhearted but dull approach to their stories.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: A crucial episode of the nineteen-sixties, centered on both the space race and the civil-rights struggle, comes to light in this energetic and impassioned drama.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: An accomplished and deftly executed movie that entertains, engages and earns your time, money and attention.
reviews.author: Simon Thompson

reviews.text: It has a few slow patches but the sheer volume of material it covers means there's always something worth paying attention to.
reviews.author: Jennie Kermode

reviews.text: Here's a crowd-pleaser that hits all the predictable notes, but you won't mind.
reviews.author: Susan G. Cole

reviews.text: Uplifting true story, delivering an inspiring message of hope...
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: An inspiring story that had to be told - and finally has been. Superb acting all around and a remarkable tale make this a big winner.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: The worthy upbeat historical film on the early pioneers of NASA never fails to point out how courageous and saintly were its three black protagonists..
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: This inspirational story of three brilliant women is like a bright ray of hope breaking out from the pre-Civil Rights South.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Hidden Figures is sensational, spirited and necessary. It reminds us not only where we've been, but how far we still have to go, and gives us signs of hope and direction.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: Although it looks like a movie machine-tooled to ride the wave of #OscarsSoWhite backlash, its actual ambitions seem far more modest: to entertain a lot, to educate a bit and to cheerlead pretty much constantly.
reviews.author: Catherine Shoard

reviews.text: This is the movie America needs right now.
reviews.author: Clay Cane

reviews.text: An Erin Brockovich-type feel-good biopic about 3 female African-American NASA math-wizard engineers who saved the 1960s Apollo rocket program and contributed to Civil Rights.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: Some sparkling performances and an inviting milieu can't completely overcome the bland trappings of a feel-good message movie. Everything in "Hidden Figures" is smoothly efficient but also a little anticlimactic and friction-less.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: The central characters' dogged refusal to cede their places on a team that keeps trying to reject them is a moving display of heroism.
reviews.author: Elise Nakhnikian

reviews.text: "Hidden Figures" is empowerment cinema at its most populist, and one only wishes that the film had existed at the time it depicts - though ongoing racial tensions and gender double-standards suggest that perhaps we haven't come such a long way, baby.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: Boy, is it a crowd pleaser
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: With spunky determination and spirit, Melfi's film manages to calculate the path to a winning formula that succeeds.
reviews.author: Rodrigo Perez

reviews.text: The highlights of "Hidden Figures" are in the two show-stopping performances of musical artist turned actress Janelle Monae and Academy Award winner Kevin Costner.
reviews.author: Clayton Davis

reviews.text: Feel-good history, but it works, and it works on behalf of heroes from a cinematically under-served community. These smart, accomplished women had the right stuff, and so does this movie.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: With an air of optimism and hope for the future, Hidden Figures is a balm for the current political landscape, inspiring audiences to stand up for their ideals and continue striving forward.
reviews.author: Robert Yaniz, Jr.

reviews.text: Great story and powerful performances in a film that dramatizes a neglected aspect of the Civil Rights movement.
reviews.author: Louis Proyect

synopsis: Three brilliant African American women at NASA -- Katherine Johnson, Dorothy Vaughan and Mary Jackson -- serve as the brains behind one of the greatest operations in history: the launch of astronaut John Glenn into orbit, a stunning achievement that restored the nation's confidence, turned around the Space Race and galvanized the world.
